Q1: Sodium nitrate has known hazards (Tier 1) for carcinogenicity, mutagenicity, or reproductive toxicity (CMR), oral toxicity (ORL), and organ/systemic toxicity (OGN). Additionally, it presents potential hazards (Tier 2) for environmental toxicity (ENV), endocrine disruption (EDC), inhalation toxicity (IHL), and dermal/eye toxicity (SKN), based on expanded scientific data.
Q2: Sodium nitrate is identified on the TEDX list as a potential endocrine disruptor and on the SCIL Yellow Triangle list for having some hazard profile issues. While it also appears on the FDA "Substances Added to Food" list, indicating low hazard in specific food additive applications, this suggests that concerns may exist for its use outside of tightly regulated, very low quantities.
Q3: Sodium nitrate is extensively characterized with over 67,000 literature references and a well-defined molecular structure. It has an above-average number of toxicity records (29) and no data-deficient (Tier 4) hazard classifications, indicating a substantial body of hazard assessment information, although it has not undergone full IRIS or PPRTV evaluation.
